issues.description: IdentityGrammar allows a sign token but never asserts it produces a single signed numeric value
issues.detail: The new (SignedSegmentGrammar optional, NumericLiteralSegment) pair parses '-1' as two separate children rather than a signed numeric literal. No invariant or comment states what the grammar guarantees, and downstream consumers reading the parse tree will see a bare minus token adjacent to a positive literal. Either wrap in a SignedLiteralSegment or document the shape explicitly.

issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor loses the top-level Delimited that allowed comma-separated clauses
issues.detail: The previous grammar wrapped the OneOf in Delimited(...), allowing 'ADD col_b ..., DROP COLUMN a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS c' in one statement. The new grammar replaces this with a bare OneOf and the corresponding fixture is deleted rather than fixed. The PR description frames this as removing an 'invalid' example, but that statement is valid T-SQL per Microsoft docs. State the invariant: one clause per ALTER TABLE, intentional.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepting NumericLiteralSegment is unmotivated and undocumented
issues.detail: The grammar now permits a numeric literal for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, but T-SQL syntax is sysname (identifier or quoted string). No test case exercises the numeric branch and no comment cites the source. Either remove the NumericLiteralSegment alternative or add a fixture plus a one-line comment pointing at the MS docs section that motivates it.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT inner Sequence wraps the CONSTRAINT keyword as optional, permitting bare object references
issues.detail: Inside the new Delimited, the 'CONSTRAINT' keyword plus IfExistsGrammar is marked optional, so the grammar will accept 'DROP foo, bar' with no CONSTRAINT keyword at all. That is broader than T-SQL allows. Make the first CONSTRAINT mandatory and only subsequent ones optional, or document why the looser form is intentional.

issues.description: No literate comment explains the structural shift from Delimited(OneOf(...)) to OneOf(...)
issues.detail: A future reader of dialect_tsql.py will see a 160-line restructure with no in-code note that the top-level Delimited was deliberately removed, nor that comma-separated DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT now live inside each branch's own Delimited. One comment block above the OneOf naming this invariant would save the next maintainer an archaeological dig.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The functional additions (table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN identifiers/N-string passwords, negative identity seeds, delimited DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT) are reasonable and well-fixtured, but the restructure of AlterTableStatementSegment silently drops the top-level Delimited and the corresponding test case rather than acknowledging the regression in expressivity. The signed-identity grammar and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric branch are added without stated invariants or sourced justification, and the diff carries no literate comment marking the structural shift for the next maintainer. Tighten the optional-CONSTRAINT inside DROP, restore or explicitly justify dropping the multi-clause ALTER TABLE form, and add one comment block stating the new invariant.
